summary: This saved practice reading found several clauses worth asking about. It uses fictional text and is not a review of a real lease.

clauses.quote: A late fee of $50 is due if rent is paid after the 5th day of the month.
clauses.plain_english: The sample charges a $50 late fee when rent is paid after the 5th. That timing may be earlier than people expect. Ask before you treat it as allowed.
clauses.why_flagged: The fee starts on the 5th, which is a short grace period.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm when a late fee can start, and whether this $50 fee can be removed or delayed?

ma_statute_citation.title: Timing of rent penalties
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: The text addresses interest or penalties for failure to pay rent; it does not resolve every kind of fee.

clauses.quote: Tenant shall pay a turnover stipend of $400 at move-in.
clauses.plain_english: A $400 turnover stipend is due at move-in. Extra move-in charges are worth asking about, because only some upfront payments are commonly allowed.
clauses.why_flagged: The stipend is an extra charge at the start of the tenancy.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm what the turnover stipend pays for, and whether it can be removed?

ma_statute_citation.title: Amounts a landlord may require at the start of a tenancy
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: Applies to residential real property. The statute permits only specified initial payments, subject to statutory exceptions and any authorized security-deposit alternative.

clauses.plain_english: The deposit is $2,400 while rent is $1,600. A deposit above one month of rent is a common reason to ask a question.
clauses.why_flagged: The deposit is larger than one month of the stated rent.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm whether the deposit can be lowered to one month of rent?

ma_statute_citation.title: Amounts a landlord may require at the start of a tenancy
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: Applies to residential real property. The statute permits only specified initial payments, subject to statutory exceptions and any authorized security-deposit alternative.

clauses.quote: Tenant shall pay a non-refundable professional cleaning fee of $250 before receiving keys.
clauses.plain_english: A non-refundable $250 cleaning fee is due before keys are handed over. Non-refundable move-in fees are worth a direct question.
clauses.why_flagged: The fee is non-refundable and due up front.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm whether this cleaning fee is required, and whether it can be removed?

ma_statute_citation.title: Amounts a landlord may require at the start of a tenancy
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: Applies to residential real property. The statute permits only specified initial payments, subject to statutory exceptions and any authorized security-deposit alternative.

clauses.quote: Landlord may enter the apartment at any time without notice.
clauses.plain_english: The sample lets the landlord enter at any time without notice. Entry rules are worth confirming before you sign.
clauses.why_flagged: The sentence gives no notice period.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm how much notice you will give before entering, except in an emergency?

ma_statute_citation.title: Entry, quiet enjoyment, and services
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: Section 14 applies to residential premises within its terms; Section 15B(1)(a) addresses permitted landlord entry before a lease ends. The statutes do not establish one general notice period for every entry.

clauses.quote: This lease renews automatically for 12 months unless Tenant gives 90 days written notice.
clauses.plain_english: The lease renews for a full year unless the tenant gives 90 days of written notice. That is a long lead time, so it is worth asking if a shorter notice is possible.
clauses.why_flagged: Automatic renewal plus a 90-day notice is easy to miss.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm the notice deadline, and whether a shorter notice period is acceptable?

clauses.quote: All tenants are jointly and severally liable for the full rent and all other charges.
clauses.plain_english: Any one tenant may be asked for the full rent, not only a share. That is a shared-risk term and worth understanding before you sign.
clauses.why_flagged: Joint and several liability is a shared-risk term, treated as worth asking about.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm that each tenant can be asked for the full rent if a roommate does not pay?

clauses.quote: The security deposit shall be held in a separate interest-bearing account.
clauses.plain_english: The sample says the deposit sits in its own interest-bearing account. That is a more ordinary protection. You can still ask for the bank name in writing.
clauses.why_flagged: Included as a contrast: this sentence is the sample's more protective clause.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm the bank name for that separate account before move-in?

ma_statute_citation.title: Security-deposit handling and tenant notices
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: Covers statutory receipt, account, interest, recordkeeping, and related requirements for residential security deposits.

clauses.plain_english: We did not find a statement of condition that describes the apartment at move-in. It may be in a page we did not read, or it may be missing.
clauses.why_flagged: No statement-of-condition sentence was found in the sample text.
clauses.question_for_landlord: Could you confirm whether you will provide a statement of condition at move-in?

ma_statute_citation.title: Statement of condition for a security deposit
ma_statute_citation.scope_note: Applies when a residential lessor accepts a security deposit; the statutory timing and tenant response period are specific.
